One pair is the minimum, because the output differs from the input by a single 39-bp insertion.\n\nThe output plasmid is the input plus `tagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaa`, inserted after position 215. That puts it just after the `atgagc…` start codon region. I checked that inserting those 39 bases into the input reproduces the output exactly.\n\n```\n>fwd\ntagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaagcaagggcgaggagctgtt\n>rev\nctcatatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttcta\n```\n\n- **Forward primer:** a 39-nt 5' tail carrying the insertion, then 18 nt that anneal to the input (`gcaagggcgaggagctgtt`). Its annealing-part Tm is 63.81 °C.\n- **Reverse primer:** 45 nt, fully annealed to the input, and the reverse complement of the sequence just before the insertion point. Its Tm is 63.81 °C.\n- **Tm gap:** the two Tm values differ by about 0.003 °C. Both come from `oligotm` with the flags you gave, computed on the annealing portions only.\n- **Annealing lengths:** 18 nt and 45 nt, both inside the 15–45 range.\n- **Layout:** the two primers sit back-to-back and don't overlap, which is the standard Q5 site-directed mutagenesis design. The kit's KLD step then re-circularizes the linear product.\n\nI picked the pair that gave the closest Tm match between the two primers. The reverse primer sits at the 45-nt limit.","time":{"start":1793305735233,"end":1793305735233}}}
